overview: Two CRISPR-based tools that repurpose a catalytically dead Cas9 to control gene expression without cutting DNA, in opposite directions.
genZNote: CRISPRi hits mute. CRISPRa hits the megaphone.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: Uses catalytically dead Cas9 (dCas9) fused to repressor domains, guided to a gene's promoter to block transcription and silence expression.
aspects.valueB: Uses dCas9 fused to transcriptional activator domains, guided to a gene's promoter to recruit transcription machinery and boost expression.

aspects.label: Effect on Transcription
aspects.valueA: Represses/decreases transcription of the target gene.
aspects.valueB: Activates/increases transcription of the target gene.

aspects.label: DNA Cutting
aspects.valueA: No DNA cutting — dCas9 lacks nuclease activity; effect is purely regulatory and reversible.
aspects.valueB: No DNA cutting — also uses dCas9, reversible and non-mutagenic.

aspects.label: Commonly Fused Effector Domains
aspects.valueA: KRAB repressor domain is the most common fusion partner.
aspects.valueB: VP64, p65, or synergistic activation mediator (SAM) complexes are common fusion partners.

aspects.label: Applications
aspects.valueA: Systematic gene knockdown screens, studying essential genes without permanently altering the genome.
aspects.valueB: Upregulating endogenous genes for functional studies or potential therapeutic gene activation.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueA: dCas9 + repressor domain silences a target gene.
aspects.valueB: dCas9 + activator domain boosts expression of a target gene.
